clue.text: When Barnet is bushy for a change

indicators.note: change here means the two little words are switched round into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A note about letting one's hair grow out for a bit of variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), so the definition describes a big, bushy hairstyle. The anagram fodder is 'for a', with 'for' doing double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a hairstyle in which naturally curly hair is grown out into a full, rounded bushy shape.

clue.text: Men of letters turned on irate doctor

parts.note: a light that is turned on is lit

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Writers round on an angry physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun for the irate person, but it is a verb telling you to tamper with the letters of irate.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are well-read, educated people, especially writers and scholars, the literary class.

clue.text: Brothers order: "Frank and Mary — embrace child!"

parts.note: frank and free both mean open and unrestrained in speech

indicators.note: the name Mary wraps its arms around the child, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An order of brothers, perhaps monks, being told by a Frank and a Mary to hug their child.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank and Mary look like two people's names; Frank is in fact the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasonry is a fraternal society whose members call one another brother, so it is an order of brothers.

clue.text: Couple with servicemen by the side of the dam

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them
RN is the Royal Navy
a can mean per, as in twice a day, and per means by
L, left, is one side

explanation.surface: A pair of soldiers or sailors strolling beside a reservoir wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The dam is not a reservoir wall but a mother animal, as in horse breeding; the slight A for 'by' runs via per.
explanation.definitionFit: Maternal means relating to a mother, and a dam is the mother of a foal or other animal.

clue.text: Woollen hat found lying under stopcock

indicators.note: in a down answer the hat sits below the other piece, so it comes second

parts.note: only the first half, stop, is used here: to ban something is to stop it; the second half, cock, is the definition
a tam (tam-o'-shanter) is a Scottish woollen bonnet

explanation.surface: A woolly hat has been discovered beneath a plumbing valve.
explanation.walkthrough: The word stopcock is split in two: stop gives one piece and cock is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic chicken, and the word is used for a bantam cock in particular.

clue.text: First, second and third of four by rank, colloquially

parts.note: chief means first or foremost

indicators.note: picks the letter in third position of the following word

parts.note: taken as written
per means by, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Listing ranks one, two and three out of four, in casual speech.
explanation.walkthrough: A chief super is the informal name for a chief superintendent, a senior British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief superintendent is a senior officer grade in British police forces, shortened in everyday talk to this form.

clue.text: Hot scarf seen on November 1st

parts.note: a stole is a long scarf worn round the shoulders

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that precedes it is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warm scarf spotted on the first of November.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot looks like a temperature for the scarf; it is the slang sense of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, so recently pinched property is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Book review said to contain them

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book of the New Testament recounting the apostles' deeds
second meaning: a revue, which sounds like review, is a show made up of separate turns

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on review and revue sounding alike: a variety revue is a string of performers' turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is named for the apostles' deeds, and a revue consists of a sequence of short performances or turns.

clue.text: Brother found by daycare centre

indicators.note: centre means keep only the middle of the word care, so its outer letters go

parts.note: day gives FRI, short for Friday, and care is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sibling discovered beside a children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daycare' splits into day and care: only the centre of care is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Brother is the title of a friar, a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Half-hearted chap ate it perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters given are one possible arrangement of something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man listlessly finishes his food, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apathetic shows little interest or enthusiasm, acting in a lukewarm way.

clue.text: Fatigue shown by public protecting old monarch

indicators.note: the word for public surrounds the other pieces as if shielding them

parts.note: overt means open, done in public view
ex means former
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Tiredness displayed by the populace as they guard an aged king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatigue is a verb here: to wear out by too much effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert is to tire oneself by strain, a verb sense of wearing out.

clue.text: He appears among the panellists

indicators.note: the man's name shows up lodged inside the letters of the next words

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man turns up in a television panel line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis is a man's first name or surname, so it can stand for a male person referred to as he.

clue.text: Strong coffee reaches new level

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A potent espresso drink achieves a new standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Level is a verb here, meaning to make flat or knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten something is to make it even and smooth, or to raze it to the ground.

clue.text: Get chef drunk in time

indicators.note: the single letter for time is placed inside the other letters
a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting the cook tipsy within the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch is to go and get something and bring it back.

clue.text: Stew tea: it's a key way to relax

indicators.note: stewing tea leaves it churning, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that brewing a strong cup of tea is the secret to unwinding.
explanation.walkthrough: Stew looks like a kitchen instruction; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning to rest, calm down and not exert oneself.

clue.text: See 3
Connect student to peasant

parts.note: to yoke animals is to join them together in harness
L is the learner plate

explanation.surface: Linking a pupil up with a farm labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country dweller, a rustic, close in sense to a peasant.

clue.text: Dumb insolence may lead to this

definitions.text: Dumb insolence may lead to this

parts.note: dumb and thick both mean stupid
lip is cheek, impudent talk

explanation.surface: Silent defiance, the military offence, can end in a punch in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumb insolence is a disciplinary term for silently showing contempt; giving lip to the wrong person can earn a swollen mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen lip is the kind of injury a punch provokes, a likely result of cheek.

clue.text: See 17
Finished with heartless acts? Make cakes!

parts.note: past means over, finished

indicators.note: the heart, or middle letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: rites are ceremonial acts

explanation.surface: Having done with cruel deeds, a person turns to baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless looks like a description of cruel acts; it tells you to drop the middle letter of the word for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are small sweet baked goods made with dough, a kind of cake.

clue.text: King stands to the right of drawing board

indicators.note: the king piece is placed after the other, to its right

parts.note: a plan is a technical drawing

explanation.surface: A monarch positioned beside a drawing board.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is a long flat piece of timber, a board.

clue.text: Defending champion?

definitions.meaning: read in the surface as a sports title holder keeping the crown; cryptically, speaking in someone's defence as a pleader does
a champion is also one who supports a cause, not only a winner

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a title holder in sport; read again, it is a champion of a cause who argues in defence, as a courtroom pleader does.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is one who publicly supports a cause, or a lawyer who pleads a client's case in court.

clue.text: Less blue or more pink (when tickled)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: less sad, blue being low in spirits
second meaning: tickled pink means delighted, so more of it is more pleased

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves look like colour comparisons; blue and tickled pink are idioms for sad and delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for glad describes someone more cheerful and in better spirits.

clue.text: Confer by river — there's nothing in the net

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: the ring for nothing is placed within the letters for the web

parts.note: WWW, the World Wide Web, is the internet
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Holding talks at the riverside after an empty fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is a meeting for discussion, so to powwow is to confer.

clue.text: Kick about the ring

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a coil is a ring or loop of rope or wire

explanation.surface: A boxer lashing out around the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Kick is the jolt of a gun when fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's recoil is its backward jolt on firing, commonly called its kick.

clue.text: Pucker up quietly — flower changes hands finally

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the closing letter swaps one hand for the other, right becoming left

parts.note: a river is something that flows, a flow-er

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a kiss as a bloom is handed over at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means something that flows, a river; R and L stand for right and left hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to wrinkle and contract, and pucker up describes skin or fruit doing the same.

clue.text: Singular warlord points to part of bow

parts.note: Lord Haw-Haw was a Second World War Nazi propagandist; taking him singly gives just one half of his name
S and E are two compass points

explanation.surface: A lone military chief indicating a section of the archery bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Haw-Haw was the nickname of William Joyce, who broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain during the war.
explanation.definitionFit: The hawse is the part of a ship's forward end, near the bows, where the anchor cables pass through.

clue.text: Carry sleeping policeman, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to lug something heavy
second meaning: a raised bump in the road, which British drivers call a sleeping policeman

explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping policeman is British slang for a speed bump, not a dozing officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hump a load is to carry it with effort, and a hump in the road is a speed bump.

clue.text: Case of paper showing concern about finger

indicators.note: the word for concern goes round the other one

parts.note: care means worry or concern
to finger something is to touch it

explanation.surface: A document case showing anxiety around a pointed digit.
explanation.walkthrough: A cartouche is also a paper cartridge case for gunpowder, the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche was a paper cartridge, a tube holding a charge of powder for a musket.

clue.text: Promise of love at hotel

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vow of devotion made at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow.

clue.text: Stable fails to complete the race

indicators.note: the race word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a race is an event in athletics

explanation.surface: A racing stable's runner doesn't finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Stable looks like a noun for horses; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means steady and level, a synonym of stable.

clue.text: A cheeky display before a Polish liquor

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare buttocks, cheeks in a cheeky sense
a shine is a polish on shoes

explanation.surface: A rude display before a vodka from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality but is the noun for buffing, shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirits, a homemade liquor.

clue.text: It reverses the charge

indicators.note: the two letters of It are written back to front

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person reversing the telephone charges, making a collect call.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to the church, a levy or charge.
